How it works

Three steps, and none of them require you to explain yourself.

  1. Step 1

    Choose a topic

    Start from a clinically grounded guide — anxiety, burnout, grief, trauma, sleep and more. Each one is written in plain language, without diagnosis or jargon.

    Nine guides, reviewed quarterly

  2. Step 2

    Dispatch anonymously

    Send the resource as a plain link by SMS or email. Your name is never attached, nothing is logged, and the link contains no identifiers or tracking parameters.

    No sender identity, no read receipts

  3. Step 3

    Support arrives gently

    They open a quiet, ad-free guide with grounding tools, coping strategies and helplines — and read it at their own pace, with no account and no follow-up.

    No sign-up, no email capture

Safety architecture

Zero retention is a design constraint, not a policy promise.

The safest data is the data that was never collected. We built dispatch so that there is nothing to leak, subpoena, or sell — and so that nobody has to trust our intentions to trust the service.

No IP logging
Requests are handled in memory and never written to a log file. We cannot tell you where a dispatch came from because we never learn it.
No accounts for recipients
A resource link opens straight into the guide. No email capture, no sign-up wall, no “verify to continue”.
No stored personal data
Phone numbers and email addresses are used once to deliver the link and are then discarded — not archived, not hashed for later.
No third-party trackers
No analytics scripts, advertising pixels, or cross-site cookies anywhere on this site, including the guides themselves.

Immediate help · 24/7

If tonight feels unsurvivable, talk to someone now.

These lines are free, confidential, and staffed around the clock. You do not need to be in danger to use them — distress is reason enough.

  • Call or text 988988 Suicide & Crisis LifelineFree, confidential support 24/7 for anyone in emotional distress — not only suicidal crisis.
  • Text HOME to 741741Crisis Text LineText-first support with a trained volunteer crisis counselor, usually within five minutes.
  • Call 1-800-662-4357SAMHSA National HelplineTreatment referrals and information for substance use and co-occurring conditions.
